chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: White trombonists: Miff Mole, Tommy Dorsey, Jack Jenney, Will Bradley, Buddy Morrow
summary: Jackson recalls white trombonists he heard, from Miff Mole through Billy Rausch and Jack Jenney across from Redman's band, to Buddy Morrow the iron man.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: There's a couple of white trombone players I know that, you know, --
Yeah, we didn't mention enough of
the white trombone players. We just touched on Jack Teagarden. We haven't mentioned -- just to digress -- we haven't mentioned Tommy, --
We haven't mentioned Tommy, we haven't mentioned Jack Janney. [handwritten correction: 'Janney' struck through, 'Jenney' written above]
And, of course, -- oh, there was a lot of good trombone players.
Miff Moe was the first, he was the first one I noticed. [handwritten correction: 'Moe' written above 'Hoe']

Of course, when I joined McKinney's band and Don had told me about Tommy because Don, when Don was writing for Whiteman, Tommy Dorsey and his brother Jimmy was in Whiteman's band. That's when I first heard about Tommy Dorsey. I didn't know nothing about him because he, you know -- Miff Moe was -- [handwritten correction: 'Moe' written above 'Hoe']

Well, black and white bands didn't get to see one another enough. We would play together but we could hear them and appreciate their great talent, of a guy like Teagarden and a guy like Miff Moe. [handwritten correction: 'Moe' written above 'Hoe']
Well, with Don's band we got to play across from Isham Jones. [handwritten correction: 'Isham' written above 'Eisam']

We got to play across from Cass Long and that's where we got to know Peewee Hunt -- he was playing there. They didn't have but two trombones when I first played across from Cass Long and Billy Rausch. Billy Rausch was a beautiful trombone player, a beautiful trombone player.
And when I first played across from Isham Jones, Jack Janney was playing trombone with Isham. You know he later played with Artie Shaw?
Then later had his own band, you know, before he died.
He was a very good trombone player, I thought, of the white -- Billy Rausch was a very good trombone player.
But I never listened to too many. There was so many good white trombone players but they weren't exactly soloists.
Oh, he was a beautiful melodic trombone player. Will Bradley.
I call him the iron man because Buddy Morrow used to play -- he had a band and he used to play the parts and the solos and never give out.
